name: Burnout Test
tagline: Find out how close you are to burning out.
intro: This test looks at the three classic signs of burnout: exhaustion, growing distance from your work and a shrinking sense of accomplishment. Answer based on how you have felt over the last month. It takes about five minutes and gives you a clear picture of where your energy is going.
seoTitle: Burnout Test – Free online burnout risk check
seoDescription: Are you heading for a burnout? Take this 5-minute test on exhaustion, cynicism and motivation and get a personal report with practical advice.

exhaustion.name: Exhaustion
exhaustion.short: How physically and emotionally drained you feel.
exhaustion.low: Your energy levels look healthy. You seem to recover well after effort and still have energy left for life outside work. Keep protecting what works for you: regular sleep, real breaks and activities that recharge you. Notice early warning signs, such as skipping lunch or working late more often, so you can adjust before your reserves run low and small habits slip.
exhaustion.mid: You are experiencing a noticeable amount of fatigue. You are still functioning, but your reserves are under pressure and recovery may take longer than it used to. This is the right moment to act. Look at where your energy goes: which tasks or situations drain you most? Plan short recovery moments during the day and guard your evenings and weekends. Small structural changes now prevent bigger problems later.
exhaustion.high: Your answers point to serious exhaustion. You may feel drained most of the time, sleep badly or find that rest no longer helps. This is a signal to take seriously. Talk to your doctor or a qualified professional about how you feel, and consider discussing your workload with your manager. Reduce what you can, ask for help and give recovery the same priority as your work. Exhaustion this strong rarely fixes itself without change.

cynicism.name: Detachment
cynicism.short: How much distance and cynicism you feel towards your work.
cynicism.low: You still feel engaged with your work and the people around you. Your work seems to mean something to you, which is one of the strongest protections against burnout. Keep investing in the parts of your job that give you a sense of purpose and in good relationships with colleagues. It also helps to notice what keeps you motivated, so you can protect it when your workload grows or your organisation goes through changes.
cynicism.mid: Some distance has crept into how you relate to your work. You might notice more irritation, less interest or a tendency to just get things done without caring much. This is often a way of protecting yourself from overload. Try to reconnect with what originally drew you to your work, and talk openly about frustrations instead of letting them build up.
cynicism.high: You seem to have pulled back strongly from your work. Cynicism, irritation or indifference can be a sign that you have been running on empty for a while. It is not a character flaw but a warning sign. Reflect on what has changed and discuss it with someone you trust. If these feelings come with low mood or exhaustion, please speak with a doctor or a qualified professional.

inefficacy.name: Reduced accomplishment
inefficacy.short: How much your sense of competence and achievement has dropped.
inefficacy.low: You still feel capable and effective. You trust your skills and see that your efforts lead to results. This confidence is a valuable buffer against stress. Keep celebrating your wins, however small, and stay aware of your limits so your high standards do not turn into overwork. Continuing to learn and taking on challenges that suit you will help you keep this sense of competence in the long run.
inefficacy.mid: Your sense of achievement is under some pressure. You may doubt yourself more often or feel that your work makes less of a difference than it used to. Write down what you actually completed each week to get a realistic view, and ask colleagues or your manager for concrete feedback. Breaking big goals into smaller steps can help you feel progress again and rebuild your confidence step by step.
inefficacy.high: You currently feel much less effective than you would like. Tasks may seem harder, mistakes more frequent and your efforts less meaningful. Often this follows from long-term exhaustion rather than a lack of ability. Be kind to yourself, lower the bar temporarily and seek support. If this feeling persists, consider talking to a coach, a doctor or another qualified professional.

summary: Burnout develops gradually across three areas: energy, engagement and sense of accomplishment. Below you see how you score on each. Higher scores mean more burnout signals. Your report is based on your answers about the past month and is not a medical diagnosis.
